duplicate_risk.evidence: The study presents original local surveillance data from Kumasi, Ghana, funded by the local EOD research working group, with no indication of sharing samples with larger consortia.

assessment.summary: The study investigated insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae s.l. (An. gambiae s.s. and An. coluzzii) from Kumasi, Ghana. Larvae were collected from irrigated vegetable farms and reared to adults. WHO tube bioassays were performed for pyrethroids, carbamates, organochlorides, and organophosphates. Genotyping was performed for Vgsc L995F (L1014F) and Ace-1 G280S (G119S) on 619 specimens. Vgsc L995F was detected at high frequencies (61% in An. gambiae s.s. and 91% in An. coluzzii), and genotype-phenotype association was reported (segregated by alive/dead). Ace-1 G280S was not detected.
